newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi Electric touts job security.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Electric touts job security.

text.p: Mitsubishi Electric Corp has adopted many American business traits but remains committed to the Japanese model of job security, Chief Executive Takashi Kitaoka told a business audience on Wednesday.
"We intend to maintain job security and do so through business development," Kitaoka told the Boston College Chief Executives Club.
Secure employment is one of the most important social contributions that companies can make, and "layoffs are contrary to our reason for being," he said.
However, the company has been cutting back headquarters staff and transferring autonomy to regions, he said.
Mitsubishi Electric has been criticized for its policy in the face of the sharp slowdown in Japan's economy, but job security increases employee loyalty and productivity, he said.

"It is estimated that Japan could lose more than one million manufacturing jobs as companies try to regain their competitive edge," Kitaoka said, "and, for the first time, many Japanese are asking: 'Is my job or pension safe?'."
Mitsubishi Electric has more than 100,000 employees worldwide, including about 50,000 in Japan, and ranks among the top 15 largest Japanese companies, a spokesman said.

Kitaoka said Mitsubishi Electric, and other Japanese companies, must adopt some American business practices -- such as encouraging creativity, promoting women and adopting a transnational outlook -- to compete in the global economy.

"Just as we are cutting back headquarters staff and transferring autonomy, so Japan must deregulate the economy and slash bureaucracies," he said. "And as we're trying to become more creative, so must Japan."
